This optional guide illustrates how to use the **same fit-and-predict
interface** with an observational RHC dataset. It is for users who already
have access to the prepared analysis files; **none are included in the
package**. New users should begin with the self-contained three-treatment,
three-response [getting-started tutorial](getting-started.html).

Before running the code, install the package and its optional `ranger`,
`survival`, and `randomForestSRC` dependencies. Keep all input and output files
in an access-controlled research workspace.

## RHC: local-data walkthrough

The original right-heart catheterization (RHC) analysis contains **two**
treatments (`No RHC`, `RHC`) and **two** response types: length of stay and
censored survival. It is included here as a brief example of adapting the
*same public functions* to a real research dataset; the three-treatment toy
example above remains the recommended starting point.

**RHC participant records are not shipped in the package.** The code below
assumes your study team has already prepared the original analysis-ready RDS
and the covariate specification CSV. Substitute your own secure file paths,
and use the research-approved cohort and preprocessing.

```{r rhc-optional, eval=FALSE}
# Files already prepared in the original RHC study; not included here.
rhc <- readRDS("PRIVATE_PATH/12_rhc_analysis_ready.rds")
spec <- read.csv("PRIVATE_PATH/01_covariate_specification.csv")
keep <- as.character(spec$included_primary) == "TRUE"
baseline <- as.character(spec$variable[keep])
stopifnot(length(baseline) == 48L,
          all(c("A_label", "los_days", "surv_time_180", "event180",
                baseline) %in% names(rhc)))
for (v in baseline) {
  if (is.character(rhc[[v]])) rhc[[v]] <- factor(rhc[[v]])
}
rhc$A_label <- factor(as.character(rhc$A_label),
                      levels = c("No RHC", "RHC"))

# Illustrative disjoint split; NOT the manuscript's outer-five-fold protocol.
set.seed(20261107)
by_arm <- split(seq_len(nrow(rhc)), rhc$A_label)
heldout_ids <- unlist(lapply(by_arm, function(ix)
  sample(ix, round(0.30 * length(ix)))))
training_ids <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(rhc)), heldout_ids)
training_ids <- sort(sample(training_ids, 1600L))
heldout_ids <- sort(sample(heldout_ids, 60L))
training <- rhc[training_ids, , drop = FALSE]
heldout <- rhc[heldout_ids, , drop = FALSE]

# Reject previously unseen factor categories rather than silently recoding.
novel <- vapply(baseline, function(v) {
  if (!is.factor(training[[v]])) return(FALSE)
  any(!as.character(heldout[[v]]) %in% as.character(training[[v]]))
}, logical(1))
if (any(novel)) stop("Unseen held-out factor levels; revise the split or preprocessing.")

rhc_outcomes <- list(
  stay = list(type = "continuous", column = "los_days",
              direction = "lower", probs = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75),
              grid_length = 9L),
  survival = list(type = "survival", time = "surv_time_180",
                  status = "event180", times = c(30, 90, 150),
                  censoring = "pooled_km", min_G = 0.05)
)
rhc_fit <- fit_dr_itr(training, "A_label", baseline, rhc_outcomes,
  weights = c(stay = 0.5, survival = 0.5),
  nuisance_folds = 2L, num.trees = 60L,
  propensity_trees = 60L, min.node.size = 10L,
  propensity_min_node_size = 50L,
  survival_outcome_learner = "rsf", survival_num.trees = 60L,
  seed = 20261107L)
# Requires optional package randomForestSRC for the RSF learner.
rhc_choices <- predict(rhc_fit, heldout[, baseline, drop = FALSE])
table(rhc_choices$best_treatment)  # Aggregate only; do not export profiles.
```

This is a **small software demonstration**, not a reproduction of the RHC
Stage 3 nested held-out study, a clinical recommendation tool, or an
independent evaluation of causal policy value. Model validity additionally
depends on exchangeability, positivity, outcome-model adequacy, and the
assumptions behind the selected censoring method. In particular,
`censoring="pooled_km"` assumes censoring independent of treatment and
covariates; it may not suit all observational studies.

## What this example does not establish

The demonstration is **not** the manuscript's outer-five-fold held-out
analysis, a prospective test, or an estimate of policy value. Use independent
validation and study-specific confounding/censoring diagnostics for substantive
analysis. Do not distribute fitted RHC models or person-level predictions.
